<p align="center"><img src="img/palantir.png" width="380" alt="PalantiR"></p>

`PalantiR` simulates and visualizes complete substitution histories --- every
substitution event, with its time, codon, and fitness context --- under
time-heterogeneous mutation--selection codon substitution models and other
advanced models, including site-specific fitness profiles, epistasis between
sites, and changes in effective population size or fitness along a phylogeny.

For installation notes, see [this page](installation.html).

Details on particular models and simulation types can be found on the
following pages:

# What's new in 1.3

Version 1.3 makes `scaling_type = "synonymous"` a dS gauge: branch lengths
measure neutral synonymous substitutions per synonymous opportunity,
equivalent to neutral nucleotide substitutions per site. The former
synonymous-event-count convention remains available as
`"synonymous-per-codon"`. Time-heterogeneous simulations preserve the chosen
currency through model shifts. See
[NEWS.md](https://github.com/dekoning-lab/PalantiR/blob/master/NEWS.md) for
the complete list, including breaking changes.

# Engine validation

The simulation engine is validated by a rerunnable notebook that separately
tests event-count gauges, the dS gauge under homogeneous and
time-heterogeneous GY94 and mutation--selection models, the stationary
distribution, and transient rescaling. Each comparison has a pre-stated
statistical criterion. Read the
[current validation report](engine_validation.html) (all tests pass under
version 1.3.0), or rerun it from a clone of the repository:

```r
# in validation/, with PalantiR installed
rmarkdown::render("engine_validation.Rmd", params = list(seed = 1))
```

For a larger event-level demonstration, the
[GY94 history-validation report](GY94_History_Validation.html) simulates 5,000
codons on a 50-taxon tree, reconstructs Goldman--Yang dN/dS from all recorded
substitutions, and visualizes the branch-specific histories. That historical
demonstration explicitly uses the `"synonymous-per-codon"` event-count gauge;
its opportunity-corrected dN/dS calculation remains valid. The executable
Jupyter notebook is retained in the repository under `validation/`.
